interactions.summary: A student presses the paradox of Cato escaping hell, and Jiang answers with a speculative class exercise: imagine Cato as one of the people who were inwardly Christian before Christ and therefore redeemable when Jesus descended to hell.

claims.claim: Jiang treats Cato's presence in Purgatory as a genuine paradox because hell was previously described as a place without free will or escape.
Jiang proposes that Cato belongs to the class of pre-Christian souls whose hearts were already oriented toward Christ before Jesus arrived historically.
Jiang says Dante later presents people who never converted outwardly but were Christian in heart and therefore could ascend to Purgatory and Paradise.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang rescues Cato by inventing a category of people who were Christian before Christianity arrived in history.
signature_moments.source_phrase: they were Christian at their heart was in the right place
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It preserves the lecture's bold move from doctrinal paradox into imaginative theology.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Jiang's label for souls who lacked formal baptism or explicit conversion but inwardly aligned themselves with Christ before his coming.

chronology_notes.note: The lecture keeps Cato's status unresolved at the level of proof and instead models Purgatory as a realm that can include inwardly Christian pre-Christian souls.
